claims.text: The baseline catalyst is a nanoscale, homogeneous equiatomic PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
A reproducible post-synthesis treatment such as thermal annealing can controllably enrich the catalyst surface in Pt.
The Pt-enrichment treatment can preserve the overall solid-solution phase.
Increasing local surface Pt concentration alters the surface electronic structure.
Local Pt enrichment weakens the binding energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Weaker binding of ethanol-oxidation intermediates reduces surface poisoning.
Local Pt enrichment lowers activation barriers for ethanol oxidation.
Reduced poisoning and lower activation barriers produce faster ethanol-oxidation turnover.
Pt-enriched catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation reaction rates than homogeneous equiatomic catalysts under identical conditions.
Pt-enriched catalysts will have lower ethanol-oxidation onset potentials than homogeneous equiatomic catalysts under identical conditions.
The proposed effect is expected under acidic aqueous ethanol-oxidation conditions at approximately 60–80 °C.
The proposed effect is expected only for moderate Pt enrichment that does not cause excessive phase segregation.
The magnitude of the activity enhancement is undetermined.
The effect of Pt enrichment on long-term catalyst stability is undetermined.
